issue.title: Scripts run from a copy of the repo act on that copy, not the main checkout
issue.body:
## Current state

A script run from a worktree, a scratch copy or a test fixture silently reads and writes the main checkout at `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` instead of the copy it was run from. `tools/bash/utils.bash` sets `DOTFILES` to that fixed path every time it is sourced, overriding any value the caller set, and 92 files source it; 7 other scripts export the same fixed path themselves. Running `tools/homebrew/generate-brewfile.bash` from a scratch copy rewrote the main checkout's `tools/homebrew/Brewfile.generated`, and `features/update/tests/test_preflight.py`, `features/update/tests/test_symlinks.py`, `tools/claude/tests/test_update.py` and `scripts/checks/link-scripts.bash` each build a throwaway `HOME` with the repo at `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` so the fixed path resolves.

## Ideal state

- A script run from any copy of the repo reads, sources and writes that copy's files, never the main checkout's
- A `DOTFILES` value set in the caller's shell does not change which checkout a script acts on
- Symlinks into `$HOME` lead only to the canonical install at `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`
- Linking from any other checkout makes no links unless the person running it explicitly asks for that

## Decisions

**Constraints**

- [bash.md: a script finds its own files from its own location, and keeps paths it points other things at separate](https://github.com/ooloth/dotfiles/blob/a29fc7e393628a39028946f44f581c598a3ebb45/tools/agents/config/standards/bash.md#L37): this work brings the repo's scripts into line with it

**Open**

No open decisions. How a person links from another checkout was settled in the approach: no flag or variable, but a `HOME` whose `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` is that checkout ([approach](https://github.com/ooloth/dotfiles/issues/198#issuecomment-6646361454)).

## Starting points

- `tools/bash/utils.bash`: line 4 sets the fixed path every script inherits
- `features/update/symlinks.bash`: creates the `$HOME` symlinks that need the canonical location
- `scripts/checks/link-scripts.bash`: shows the throwaway-`HOME` setup the tests need today

nodes.body: `tools/bash/utils.bash` now loads private values from `${DOTFILES}/private.env` when a script starts with none in its environment (#230). That file is ignored, so only the main checkout has it. When this issue makes `DOTFILES` follow the checkout a script runs from, that fallback must keep reading the main checkout's `private.env`, or a script started outside zsh from a worktree, such as a Rex tab, loses every private value.

`scripts/checks/linting.bash` now has a second fallback to the main checkout's `private.env` (`a076d181`, #230). When its shell has no `PRIVATE_*` values, it loads `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles/private.env` before the private values check. It names that path itself, because its own `DOTFILES` is the checkout it runs from. Like the `utils.bash` fallback in the comment above, it must keep reading the main checkout's file, since a worktree has no `private.env`.

# Approach

After this, a script run from a worktree or a scratch copy runs that copy's code and writes only into that copy, so you can try a change before committing it without touching `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`. Links in `$HOME` and private values still come from `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`, and the link step refuses to change `$HOME` from any other checkout.

How it works:

- **Own files.** Every script that is run sets `DOTFILES` from its own location, ignoring any value the caller exported.
- **Install path.** A separate fixed path, `${HOME}/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`, is used for only two things: the link step (link targets, check mode, the broken-link sweep) and `private.env`.
- **Link guard.** Before writing, the link step checks that the checkout it runs from resolves to that install path. If not, it stops and says why.
- **Check over every script.** A check fails on any bash script that reads `DOTFILES` before setting it from its own location.
- **Recorded for the port.** Both rules go into `docs/invariants/tools.md`. The Python port (#203) already lists that file as a constraint, so the ported scripts keep the rules.

## What a good fix must achieve 🎯

| | Property | Category |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | A script run from any copy sources, reads and writes only that copy's files, whatever `DOTFILES` the caller exported. Checked over every script | 🛡️ Safety |
| P2 | Every link the link step makes in `$HOME` names a path under `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` | 🛡️ Safety |
| P3 | Run from a checkout that does not resolve to `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`, the link step changes nothing in `$HOME` and says why | 🛡️ Safety |
| P4 | A script started outside zsh from a copy still loads private values from `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles/private.env` | 🛡️ Safety |
| P5 | Run from the install, `u`, `symlinks`, `dcheck`, Amp orb setup and the link-scripts check give the same results as today | 🛡️ Safety |
| P6 | Trying a change to any script except the link step needs no throwaway `HOME` | 🙂 Experience |

**Not binding:**

- **Performance.** Resolving a script's location costs a few milliseconds per script (200 runs took 0.7 s under bash 3.2). `u` waits on `brew` calls that take hundreds of milliseconds each.

## Assumptions 🤔

- **The Python port is not close to done.** #204 has to land before any category can move, and its design is paused waiting on the start-command question. #210, which retires `utils.bash`, comes last. If the whole port were days away, folding this into it would win.

## Constraints 🧱

- **Orbs link the install path to the checkout.** In Amp orbs, `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` is a symlink to the working checkout, so the guard compares resolved paths.
- **Link text has to stay the same.** Check mode compares link text exactly, and the sweep finds repo links by their text prefix. So links have to keep naming `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`, not whatever path the script was started from.

## Options ⚖️

| Option | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | P6 | Leaves behind |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **🏆 Own-location `DOTFILES`, separate install path for links and `private.env`, guarded link step (chosen)** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| The chosen option plus a flag or variable that lets the link step write from another checkout | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ a CLI contract no current caller uses |
| Change nothing in bash, and let the Python port bring the rule | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| `utils.bash` refuses to run when the script sourcing it is outside `DOTFILES` | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Only make `DOTFILES` follow the script's location | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |

## Decided by 🧭

I tried the last option in a scratch copy:

- Main checkout's `Brewfile.generated` was no longer written.
- But `symlinks` pointed every `~/.claude` link at the copy, which disappears when the copy is deleted.
- Check mode reported the real, correct links as `WRONG TARGET`.
- No private values loaded. The existing `test_private_env.py` caught this; the other 574 tests passed.

The refusal option stops the harm but makes copies unusable, and running a copy is what worktrees and agents' scratch copies are for.

Waiting for the port leaves scripts silently acting on the main checkout until #210 lands. The bash change it avoids is mostly a one-line edit in each script, and the port rewrites those files anyway. The concepts it needs (the install path and the guard) carry straight into Python.

The opt-in adds a contract nothing uses today. The tests, the link-scripts check and orb setup already ask explicitly: they give the link step a `HOME` whose `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` is the checkout they mean. Adding a flag later is cheap, so leaving it out can be reversed.

## Deferred ⏳

- **Throwaway `HOME`s in the bash tests.** After this change, the tests that don't link anything no longer need to place the repo at `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` inside a fake `HOME`. But #203 rewrites all of them to import Python, so editing them now would be thrown away. The ticket's ideal-state bullet about tests belongs with the port.

# Design

`tools/bash/utils.bash` is the one place every script learns where it is. It names two paths:

- **`DOTFILES_INSTALL`**, fixed at `${HOME}/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`.
- **`DOTFILES`**, the checkout that `utils.bash` itself sits in, ignoring anything the caller exported. When that checkout resolves to the install, `DOTFILES` is spelled as the install path. So link text stays `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles/...` however the script was started, including in an Amp orb, where the install path is a symlink to the working checkout.

Every script sources `utils.bash` by a path relative to itself, so its own files come from its own checkout. Private values load from the install's `private.env`.

The places that write in `$HOME` all call one guard before acting: `symlink()` and the two broken-link sweeps. The guard refuses unless `DOTFILES` is the install, so a copy can never change `$HOME`.

What carries what:

- **Structure:** one place sets both paths.
- **Runtime checks:** the guard, and one assertion on the computed path.
- **Tests:** an end-to-end run from a copy, plus a check over every script that keeps the sourcing pattern in place.

The work is two commits:

1. Add the install path, the guard and the `private.env` change. From the install, nothing changes.
2. Make `DOTFILES` follow each script.

## Types 🧬

The change adds no types and changes no signatures. It changes how two shell variables are set and adds one guard function, `require_install_checkout`.

**Changes considered:**

| Option | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 | P5 | P6 | Leaves behind |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **🏆 `utils.bash` spells `DOTFILES` as the install path when the checkout is the install; `link.bash` files unchanged (chosen)** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Every `link.bash` names its sources with `${DOTFILES_INSTALL}` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ two path variables every link step author must choose between, and a check that link sources use the right one |
| `symlink()` rewrites each source from the running checkout to the install path | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ link text differs from the argument passed, and check mode and the sweep must repeat the same rewrite |

**Decided by what each leaves behind.** All three deliver every property.

- **Second variable in every `link.bash`:** a `link.bash` that uses `${DOTFILES}` by habit still works on the Mac. It only makes differently spelled links in an orb, so it would need a check of its own.
- **Rewriting inside `symlink()`:** the link no longer says what the caller asked for, and two other functions would have to repeat the rewrite.
- **Chosen option:** the spelling rule lives in one place, and the 28 `link.bash` files and the template stay as they are.

**What each piece rules out:**

- **`DOTFILES_INSTALL` is set unconditionally.** Nothing in the environment can move where links lead or where `private.env` is read. (P2, P4)
- **`DOTFILES` comes from `utils.bash`'s own location.** A caller's exported value can no longer pick the checkout. (P1)
- **Install spelling when the checkout resolves to the install.** The same checkout can no longer produce two spellings of link text, so check mode and the sweep's prefix match keep working from an orb. (P2, P5)
- **Each script sources `utils.bash` relative to itself.** Nothing is read through `${DOTFILES}` before it has been set from the script's own location. (P1, P6)
- **The guard sits at every place that writes in `$HOME`.** A copy cannot reach a `$HOME` write without passing it. (P3)

## Assertions 🛡️

The shell has no types. So whether the computed path is right, and whether a write site is allowed to act, are checked at runtime.

- **Assertion: `${DOTFILES}/tools/bash/utils.bash` exists after `DOTFILES` is computed.** Only a mistake in the path arithmetic can break this, for example a wrong number of `..`. Sourcing then stops with a message naming the computed path, instead of every later path silently pointing at nothing. This pins the positive space. The negative space (a caller's value leaking through) has no runtime signal, so the tests cover it.
- **Boundary validation: `require_install_checkout`.** It is called by `symlink()` in both modes, by `remove_broken_symlinks` and by `remove_broken_repo_symlinks`. Running from a copy is a legitimate thing for a person to do, not a bug. So the guard returns non-zero and names both paths, plus how to link from the copy on purpose (a `HOME` whose `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` is that checkout). It does not abort. It replaces the sweep's existing "`DOTFILES` must be absolute" check, which it covers because the install path is always absolute.

## Telemetry 📡

Nothing needs recording. Whether a script used the copy or the install shows in the paths it prints. A refusal names both checkouts and exits non-zero.

## Tests 🧪

Nothing at runtime notices a script that reads `${DOTFILES}` before setting it, or a caller's value leaking through. Those are the failures that act silently on the wrong checkout, so they need tests.

**Dimensions the behaviour varies along:**

- **How the checkout relates to the install:** it is the install, it is reached through a symlink to the install, or it is a copy.
- **What the caller exported:** nothing, or another checkout.
- **Which `$HOME` write site is involved:** `symlink()` writing, `symlink()` in check mode, or either sweep.

| Expectation | Property | Technique |
|---|---|---|
| A script inside a copy defines its helpers from the copy's files and writes into the copy. A second checkout named by the caller's `DOTFILES`, and a third at the `HOME` install path, are both left untouched | P1, P6 | Integration |
| Sourced through the install path, or through a real path that the install symlinks to, `DOTFILES` is spelled as the install path | P2, P5 | Example |
| From a copy, `DOTFILES` is the copy's own path | P1 | Example |
| From a checkout that is not the install, each of the four `$HOME` write sites changes nothing, exits non-zero and names both paths | P3 | Example (one subtest per site) |
| From a copy, a real `link.bash` run end to end leaves `HOME` empty | P3 | Integration |
| A script started outside zsh from a copy loads the install's `private.env` (existing `test_a_script_with_no_private_values_in_its_environment_reads_them_from_the_file`, which the naive fix failed) | P4 | Example |
| No script under `tools/` or `features/` assigns `DOTFILES` or reads it before sourcing `utils.bash` relative to itself. The check fails if it finds no scripts | P1 (checked over every script) | Static check |
| The existing link, sweep and update tests and `scripts/checks/link-scripts.bash` pass unchanged | P5 | Existing suite |

Why each technique fits:

- **Integration:** the behaviour is about which files on disk get read and written. Only a real copy with decoy checkouts shows that. Bash 3.2 reports which file defined a function (`shopt -s extdebug; declare -F`), so the test can see where the helpers came from. Before the fix, the helpers come from the decoy install, so the test fails on that assertion, not on setup.
- **Example:** each case is one concrete arrangement of paths, and the cases above cover every value of each dimension.
- **Static check:** P1 can be broken by any script, including ones added later. Only a scan of every file catches a new one. It lives in `tools/bash/tests/` so the existing test run picks it up.
- **Existing suite:** P5 is about today's behaviour from the install, which those tests already pin.

**Fixtures run once:**

- The spelling logic gave the install spelling via the install path and via the orb-style symlink, and the copy's own path from a copy.
- The probe in a copy, with both decoys present, sourced the copy's helpers and wrote only into the copy, under `/bin/bash` 3.2.
- `generate-brewfile.bash` cannot be the end-to-end subject: it uses `mapfile`, and CI's bash 3.2 lacks it. It gets checked by hand during verification instead.

**Not tested, with reasons:**

- **`features/ralph/loop.py` changing to `Path(__file__).parent`:** the expression is the whole change, and a test would only restate it.
- **The `ng` alias running `bash` instead of `zsh`:** if it is wrong, `ng` fails the moment it runs.

**Manual checks:** `dcheck` and `symlinks` get run from the install before and after the change, and their output compared (P5).

## Recorded rules 📜

These go in `docs/invariants/tools.md`, as two new list items:

- A script run from any checkout of this repo, such as a worktree or a scratch copy, sources, reads and writes that checkout's files. `tools/bash/utils.bash` sets `DOTFILES` from its own location, ignoring any value the caller exported, and every script under `tools/` and `features/` sources it by a path relative to itself before reading `DOTFILES`. `tools/bash/tests/test_dotfiles_location.py` checks every script.
- Every link the link step makes in `$HOME` names a file under `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` (`DOTFILES_INSTALL` in `tools/bash/utils.bash`), and `private.env` is read from there. Run from any other checkout, the link step, check mode included, changes nothing in `$HOME` and says why. A test or an Amp orb links from another checkout by giving it a `HOME` whose `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` resolves to that checkout.

# Design change after review

A review of `09c2958e`, `29f3740e` and `a30aef3a` found gaps that change the design above. The main one: an `update.bash` or `install.bash` run from a copy exits 1 at its link step, which skips the rest of the update (`node`'s Corepack update, `neovim`'s dependencies). From now on, a copy skips the link step with a note and carries on.

A new `is_install_checkout` in `tools/bash/utils.bash` holds the one test of whether `DOTFILES` is the install, using `-ef`. `require_install_checkout` uses it and keeps refusing. A new `run_link_step` uses it and skips. Update and install scripts reach their link step only through `run_link_step`, and `dcheck` asks once before its link loop instead of letting every `link.bash` refuse. Structure carries the single "is this the install" test, the guard is the runtime check, a static check covers every script including future ones, and integration tests cover the behaviour from a copy.

The approach's properties P1 to P6 still apply. This change adds:

| | Property | Category |
|---|---|---|
| P7 | An `update.bash` or `install.bash` run from a copy runs every step except its link step, says it skipped that step, and exits as it would have without the link step | 🙂 Experience |
| P8 | `dcheck` run from a copy reports the refusal once, in words that are true for a check | 🙂 Experience |
| P9 | The static check fails on any script in scope that reaches the install by a fixed path, assigns `DOTFILES` in any spelling, or has an update or install script run `link.bash` directly | 🛡️ Safety |

## Types 🧬

There are no types; this is bash. One predicate (`is_install_checkout`) and one function (`run_link_step <link.bash>`) are added to `tools/bash/utils.bash`.

**Changes considered:**

| Option | P3 | P5 | P7 | P9 | Leaves behind |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **🏆 `run_link_step <link.bash>` in `utils.bash`, called by `update_and_symlink`, `install_and_symlink` and the four direct callers (btop, yazi, zsh, vscode) (chosen)** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `if is_install_checkout; then …; else note; fi` written at each of the six sites | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ six copies of the branch and its message |
| A variable that makes `require_install_checkout` return 0 with a note, set by update and install scripts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ a mode on the guard, close to the opt-in the approach rejected |

**Decided by what each leaves behind.** All three deliver the properties.

- **Inline branches:** the skip message would live in six places.
- **Mode variable:** it turns the guard into something that can be switched off.
- **Chosen option:** keeps the branch in one place, and leaves the guard unconditional.

**What each piece rules out:**

- **`is_install_checkout` uses `[[ "${DOTFILES}" -ef "${DOTFILES_INSTALL}" ]]`:** the install can no longer refuse itself when reached by a path that differs in case or symlinks. Before, comparing two `cd -P` strings refused `/users/...` on macOS. The spelling rule and the guard share this one test. (P5)
- **`require_install_checkout` calls the predicate:** its message now says links are made and checked only from the install, which is true for check mode and the sweeps too. Before, it said "Not linking" in every case. (P3, P8)
- **`run_link_step` skips from a copy:** from a copy it prints one note naming the `link.bash` and the install, then returns 0. From the install it runs the `link.bash`. (P3, P7)
- **`dcheck` checks once:** it calls `require_install_checkout` before its link loop. On refusal it counts one failure and skips the loop. Before, it printed the refusal once per `link.bash`, 26 times. (P8)
- **`tools/pi/link.bash` gets the guard:** the guard now runs before its hand-written `AGENTS.md` link. Before, only the order of the lines kept a copy from making that link. (P3)
- **`tools/claude/cc.bash`:** it switches to the standard relative source line, so the static check can apply to it. (P9)

## Assertions 🛡️

The shell can't enforce "this is the install". It stays a boundary check, the guard, because running from a copy is a legitimate thing for a person to do. Nothing new needs an assertion: the existing check that `utils.bash` exists still covers the path arithmetic.

## Telemetry 📡

- **The skip note:** someone looking at a script's input and output can't tell that an update skipped its link step, so the note records which `link.bash` was skipped and why.
- **Everything else:** it is visible in exit codes and the refusal message.

## Tests 🧪

Types and assertions don't cover which checkout a script reads and writes, whether an update from a copy finishes, or whether future scripts follow the sourcing rule. These are failures that act silently or grow with the repo.

| Expectation | Property | Technique |
|---|---|---|
| Sourced through a case-swapped spelling of the install, `DOTFILES` is spelled as the install path (skipped where the filesystem is case-sensitive) | P5 | Example |
| A probe in a copy that overwrites a file all three checkouts hold changes only the copy's file, and both decoys' contents are byte-identical afterwards | P1 | Integration |
| From a copy, a script that calls `run_link_step` and then prints a marker exits 0, prints the marker, names the skipped script and the install, and leaves `HOME` empty | P3, P7 | Integration |
| Through a `HOME` whose install is a symlink to the copy, the same script makes the links | P2, P7 | Integration |
| `dcheck` in a copy with two `link.bash` files exits 1, prints the refusal exactly once, and reports no link line | P8 | Integration |
| The static check fails on a script with no `DOTFILES` that sources the install path; on `declare -x`, `readonly`, `local` and `; DOTFILES=` assignments; and on an `update.bash` or `install.bash` that runs `link.bash` directly. It passes on every script in the tree | P9 | Example + static check |
| The existing suite, `link-scripts.bash`, and `dcheck` and `symlinks` from the install are unchanged | P5 | Existing suite |

- **Example:** each case is one concrete path or one line spelling.
- **Integration:** these behaviours are about which files on disk get read and written, and only real copies with decoys show that.
- **Static check:** P9 can be broken by any script added later, and only a scan over every file catches that.

**Not tested, with reasons:**

- **The `pi` guard:** the `symlink()` calls above it already stop a copy, so a test would pass with or without the fix.
- **`VERBOSE` passing through `run_link_step`:** if it is lost, the only effect is quieter output, which shows at once.

## Recorded rules 📜

These replace the two `DOTFILES` bullets in `docs/invariants/tools.md`:

- A bash script directly in a `tools/<tool>/` or `features/<feature>/` folder, `tools/@new/` included, run from any checkout of this repo such as a worktree or a scratch copy, sources, reads and writes that checkout's files. The one exception is `private.env`, which comes from the install (next item). `tools/bash/utils.bash` sets `DOTFILES` from its own location, ignoring any value the caller exported, and each such script sources it by a path relative to itself before reading `DOTFILES`. Outside this rule are the files `utils.bash` itself sources (`tools/bash/` and `tools/macos/utils.bash`), `tools/amp/workspace-resume.bash` (which sets up the install), the setup `.zsh` files and the `wip/` drafts. `tools/bash/tests/test_dotfiles_location.py` checks that each script in scope sources `utils.bash` that way before anything else, assigns no `DOTFILES`, and names no install path.
- Every link the link step makes in `$HOME` names a file under `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` (`DOTFILES_INSTALL` in `tools/bash/utils.bash`), and `private.env` is read from there. Run from any other checkout, the link step, check mode included, changes nothing in `$HOME` and says why. An `update.bash` or `install.bash` reaches its link step only through `run_link_step`, which from another checkout skips it with a note and lets the rest of the script run. A test or an Amp orb links from another checkout by giving it a `HOME` whose `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` resolves to that checkout.

The design change above shipped in 64df7bc8 and b11b3aee. 27ce0732 then added four things that design did not show:

- **A test of the shared helper.** The static check sees only literal `bash …link.bash` lines in `update.bash` and `install.bash` files, so a change to how `update_and_symlink` runs the link step would have passed it. `tools/bash/tests/test_dotfiles_location.py` now runs the real `update_and_symlink` from a copy and checks that the link step is skipped with a note, the script carries on and exits 0, and nothing in `HOME` or the decoy checkouts changes. Putting back the old `bash -c "VERBOSE=true …"` line fails it. (P7)
- **The add-tool skill's verify step.** It said to rerun `install.bash` from the install to make the links, but `install_and_symlink` stops early when the tool is already installed, so that made none. It now says to run `features/update/symlinks.bash <tool>` once the tool is in the main checkout.
- **`docs/invariants/tools.md`.** The list of what the test checks now includes "runs no `link.bash` directly from an `update.bash` or `install.bash`".
- **`docs/standards/symlinks.md`.** The Should on hand-rolled `ln` now says it has to call `require_install_checkout` first, as `tools/pi/link.bash` does.

- `tools/bash/utils.bash`: line 4 sets the fixed path every script inherits
- `features/update/symlinks.bash`: creates the `$HOME` symlinks that need the canonical location
- `scripts/checks/link-scripts.bash`: shows the throwaway-`HOME` setup the tests need today

## Current state

A script run from a worktree, a scratch copy or a test fixture silently reads and writes the main checkout at `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` instead of the copy it was run from. `tools/bash/utils.bash` sets `DOTFILES` to that fixed path every time it is sourced, overriding any value the caller set, and 92 files source it; 7 other scripts export the same fixed path themselves. Running `tools/homebrew/generate-brewfile.bash` from a scratch copy rewrote the main checkout's `tools/homebrew/Brewfile.generated`, and `features/update/tests/test_preflight.py`, `features/update/tests/test_symlinks.py`, `tools/claude/tests/test_update.py` and `scripts/checks/link-scripts.bash` each build a throwaway `HOME` with the repo at `Repos/ooloth/dotfiles` so the fixed path resolves.

## Ideal state

- A script run from any copy of the repo reads, sources and writes that copy's files, never the main checkout's
- A `DOTFILES` value set in the caller's shell does not change which checkout a script acts on
- The tests run against the checkout they live in without building a throwaway `HOME`
- Symlinks into `$HOME` lead only to the canonical install at `~/Repos/ooloth/dotfiles`
- Linking from any other checkout makes no links unless the person running it explicitly asks for that

## Decisions

**Constraints**

- [bash.md: a script finds its own files from its own location, and keeps paths it points other things at separate](https://github.com/ooloth/dotfiles/blob/a29fc7e393628a39028946f44f581c598a3ebb45/tools/agents/config/standards/bash.md#L37): this work brings the repo's scripts into line with it

**Open**

- How does a person tell the link step to link from a checkout other than the canonical install? (new CLI contract)
